channel.title: VICEVERSA — GTA VI news and trivia
channel.description: VICEVERSA: news, timeline and trivia about Grand Theft Auto VI — Extended Look, leaks, pre-orders and a countdown to launch. Follow @vvviceversaa on X and Instagram, @vvviceversa on TikTok and @vvViceVersa on YouTube.

item.title: GTA 6 Launches in One Month: Everything You Need to Know Before November 19
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: The wait for Grand Theft Auto VI is almost over. With one month remaining until its scheduled release, Rockstar Games is entering the final stretch of its…
item.content:encoded:
The wait for Grand Theft Auto VI is almost over. With one month remaining until its scheduled release, Rockstar Games is entering the final stretch of its marketing campaign for one of the most anticipated video games in recent years.

Set in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida, the game returns players to a modern version of Vice City. This time, the story follows Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, two protagonists whose involvement in a criminal conspiracy puts them at the center of a much larger conflict.

The game is scheduled to launch on November 19, 2026, for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Before release day arrives, here's how GTA 6 reached this point and what has been confirmed so far.

From Early Leaks to the First Official Trailer

Rockstar confirmed in February 2022 that development on the next Grand Theft Auto game was underway. Later that year, in September, a major leak exposed early development footage, offering the first substantial look at the project and revealing scenes featuring the game's protagonists.

The first official trailer arrived on December 4, 2023, a day earlier than planned, after the video leaked online. It introduced the modern-day Vice City setting, offered a glimpse of Leonida's wider environment, and established an initial release window of 2025.

The trailer quickly became a major online event, drawing enormous attention from gaming communities and introducing a broader audience to Jason and Lucia. It also established the visual style and atmosphere that would define Rockstar's next open-world release.

Two Delays Changed the Release Schedule

In May 2025, Rockstar announced that GTA 6 would no longer launch in 2025. The company moved the release date to May 26, 2026, explaining that additional development time was needed to deliver the level of quality players expected.

Four days later, Rockstar released the second trailer, which expanded on the game's story, introduced additional characters, and showed more of the world surrounding Jason and Lucia.

A second delay followed in November 2025, moving the launch to November 19, 2026. Rockstar said the extra time would allow the development team to finish the game to the standard the studio was aiming for.

With the latest date approaching, the focus has shifted from the development timeline to the final promotional campaign and the features players will experience at launch.

What the Latest Trailers Have Revealed

Rockstar released an expanded presentation in August 2026, providing another look at the game's world and complementing information shared in previous trailers.

On October 15, the studio released the official launch trailer. The footage revisits Jason and Lucia and offers additional glimpses of the criminal world, locations, and characters that shape the story.

The trailer also features “Flower in a Hurricane,” an original musical collaboration involving Justice, Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard.

While the promotional material has provided plenty of details about the setting and narrative, there is still a distinction between cinematic footage and actual gameplay. Players will need to experience the finished game to assess its mechanics, mission structure, and open-world systems in full.

Preorders, Pricing, and Platforms

Preorders opened on June 25, 2026. Rockstar's digital store lists the Standard Edition at $79.99, alongside an Ultimate Edition that includes additional content.

The game is confirmed for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar has not announced an official release date for the PC version, despite ongoing speculation about a potential launch in 2027.

For console players purchasing digital copies, preload is scheduled to begin on November 12, one week before launch. Preloading allows players to download the game files in advance, although availability and timing may vary by platform and purchase.

Players should check their preferred digital storefront for the latest pricing, edition details, and download instructions.

What to Expect on November 19

With the release date approaching, the biggest questions concern how the finished game will bring Leonida to life. Players will be exploring a modern Vice City, following Jason and Lucia's story, and discovering how the different parts of the open world connect.

Rockstar's trailers have established the setting, introduced key characters, and outlined the central conflict. However, many aspects of the gameplay experience will only become clear once players can get their hands on the final release.

The PC release timeline also remains uncertain, leaving console players as the confirmed audience for launch day.

For now, November 19 is the date to watch. After years of announcements, delays, and speculation, Grand Theft Auto VI is scheduled to arrive on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S in just one month.

Correction (October 19, 2026): An earlier version of this article said the first trailer was released on December 5, 2023, and that the second trailer came out alongside the May 2025 delay announcement. Rockstar released the first trailer on December 4, 2023, a day early after it leaked, and the second trailer arrived on May 6, 2025, four days after the delay was announced.

item.title: GTA VI Enters the Final Phase of Development: Bug Fixes and an Effort to Limit Crunch
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: Rockstar Games appears to be entering the final stages of development on Grand Theft Auto VI. During a visit to the studio in late September, Bloomberg…
item.content:encoded:
Rockstar Games appears to be entering the final stages of development on Grand Theft Auto VI. During a visit to the studio in late September, Bloomberg journalist Jason Schreier reported on the team's progress, offering a glimpse into how the highly anticipated game is taking shape ahead of its planned November 19 release.

One of the clearest signs of progress can be seen on monitors throughout the studio. They display a color-coded overview of the game's bugs, with red blocks representing unresolved issues and green ones indicating problems that have been fixed. According to the report, the balance has been shifting in the right direction, suggesting that developers are resolving issues faster than new ones are being identified.

That doesn't mean development is entirely finished. Phil Hooker, one of the three executives who lead the game's development, noted that a project of this scale continues to evolve even during its final months. Small adjustments and refinements are still being made as the team works to ensure the game is ready for release.

The reported progress is only part of the story. Rockstar has also been trying to move away from the demanding work culture associated with some of its earlier productions. During the development of Red Dead Redemption 2, reports of 60-hour working weeks drew attention to the industry's reliance on so-called crunch — periods of intense overtime before a game's release.

The current approach appears to be different. Since 2024, employees have been required to work from the office five days a week, a policy reportedly adopted for security and productivity reasons, including reducing the risk of leaks. Even with that requirement, the studio is seeking to manage workloads without returning to the excessive hours that have drawn criticism in the past. Still, Rockstar executive Jennifer Kolbe acknowledged to Bloomberg that the process wasn't perfect and that some employees will say they crunched, though she described it as better than on Red Dead Redemption 2.

For fans, the steady progress on bug fixes is encouraging, although it doesn't guarantee that the release schedule will remain unchanged. Rockstar is still targeting November 19 for GTA VI, and the coming weeks will be crucial as the team works through the remaining issues and prepares the game for launch.

Correction (October 19, 2026): an earlier version of this article called Phil Hooker the game's co-director, described the crunch on Red Dead Redemption 2 as weeks exceeding 60 hours and presented the five-day office rule as part of the effort to reduce crunch. In fact, Hooker is one of the three executives who lead development, Bloomberg reported 60-hour weeks, and the office rule dates from 2024 and was adopted for security and productivity reasons.

item.title: GTA 6: Launch Trailer Reveals Jason's Past, Photorealistic Graphics, and Heavyweight Original Soundtrack
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: If the first trailer gave us a taste of the chaos in the state of Leonida, this new footage shines the spotlight directly on Jason and Lucia's past…
item.content:encoded:
If the first trailer gave us a taste of the chaos in the state of Leonida, this new footage shines the spotlight directly on Jason and Lucia's past, confirming details that position the title as a clear favorite for Game of the Year. Below, we break down the trailer's main highlights.

Jason's Dark Past and the Couple's Dynamic

One of the biggest reveals in the video is the deepening of Jason's backstory, which until now was a greater mystery than Lucia's. Right at the beginning of the trailer, we hear a monologue from the character explaining what pushed him into a life of crime: "I got into some trouble in the military. Didn't leave there on the best of terms. They don't give loans or anything like that to guys like me." Never-before-seen footage shows him working at a marina for a character named Brian, polishing boats before receiving a call from Lucia—possibly the moment he is summoned to pick her up from prison.

The duo's relationship gains new layers of depth. The trailer showcases moments of tension and intimacy, including a romantic scene in the shower, proving that mutual trust will be the core of the narrative. In an emblematic dialogue, Lucia asks, "Is everything going to be alright?" to which a protective Jason replies, "We got through everything together. We just need to get through this."

Graphical Leap and the Impressive "Sweat System"

The video makes a point to display a "captured on PS5" disclaimer, and the level of detail justifies the current-generation console exclusivity. The graphics engine's photorealism is pushed to the limit, visible in the confirmation of the rumored new "sweat system." In one scene, an NPC is shown working out intensely, and the dynamically dripping sweat highlights Rockstar's meticulous attention to detail.

Alongside the high-speed pursuits and frantic shootouts traditional to the franchise, the trailer features gorgeous landscapes ranging from murky swamps to the contemporary neon lights of a reimagined Vice City.

Heavyweight Soundtrack: Justice, Tame Impala, and SZA

Rockstar's musical curation strikes again. The trailer's rhythm is dictated by the unreleased track "Flower in a Hurricane," produced by the acclaimed French electronic duo Justice, featuring colossal guest appearances by Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard.

The partnership goes beyond marketing: the developer confirmed that Justice is composing the original score for the entire game. The track is part of Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, a record featuring 34 original songs that is already available for pre-order on physical vinyl and CD editions.

Imminent Launch and The Game Awards 2026

We are in the endgame. With the premiere locked in for November 19, 2026, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, players who secured the digital version will be able to start pre-loading data on November 12. Unfortunately for computer players, a PC release date remains unannounced.

One detail that stirred the industry was the strategic release window: November 19 allows GTA 6 to compete for the coveted Game of the Year (GOTY) statuette at The Game Awards 2026, whose eligibility rules cover titles released up until November 20.

As Rob Nelson, co-head of Rockstar North, told IGN: "The game is so big, I don't know that there's anybody on the team that knows all of it." If the launch trailer is an accurate indicator of the final experience, Rockstar is about to break every record in the industry. Once again.

Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article paraphrased Rob Nelson's quote. His exact words, from an interview with IGN, are now quoted above.

item.title: Only 34 Days Until GTA 6: New Trailer, Physical Map, and Rockstar's Promising Future
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: The Launch Trailer: Jason's Past and PS5 Action Released today, the new 1-minute and 30-second launch trailer focuses on Jason and Lucia's narrative. The…
item.content:encoded:
The Launch Trailer: Jason's Past and PS5 Action

Released today, the new 1-minute and 30-second launch trailer focuses on Jason and Lucia's narrative. The video reveals details about Jason's troubled past, seemingly leaving the military under difficult circumstances, and features an intense shower scene with Lucia, who is seen wearing her now-iconic ankle monitor.

Instead of focusing purely on gameplay, the trailer highlights the cinematic action players will experience in the vast open world. Rockstar also emphasized its partnership with Sony, confirming the footage was "captured on PS5" and reinforcing the message that the game "plays best on PS5."

The Map Returns: A Physical Media Bonus

For the nostalgics and collectors out there, possible good news has surfaced from a GameStop store. Even as the industry shifts heavily toward digital formats, a single unverified sign at one GameStop store in Pennsylvania suggests that the "physical media" copies of GTA 6 (which will actually contain digital codes in the box) will include a "physical collector's map." Rockstar, Take-Two and GameStop have not confirmed it, so treat it as a rumor for now.

Rockstar has a long-standing tradition of including printed city maps in their physical game editions, and it seems this custom will survive the digital age. Those who purchase this version at physical retail stores will also be able to pick up the box early on November 12, just in time to preload the game for the big launch on November 19.

Rockstar's Future: The End of 8-Year Waits

If the more than decade-long wait since GTA V (or the 8 years since Red Dead Redemption 2) tested fans' patience, Rockstar has a reassuring message: this shouldn't happen again.

In a recent Bloomberg report, Rockstar executives Phil Hooker and Aaron Garbut suggested that the company's next major game should come faster, though they did not give a timeline. The reason? All the technological advancements, new creation tools, and the modernized graphics engine built specifically for the ambitions of GTA 6 will allow the team to work much faster moving forward. With a workforce that has almost doubled since the release of RDR2—Bloomberg reported 4,711 employees across 12 studios, up from 2,441 at the time—the company's infrastructure has never been more robust.

With only 34 days left until we return to Vice City, the expectation is that GTA 6 will not only redefine the current industry standard but also pave the way for Rockstar's next blockbusters to reach our hands much sooner.

Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article treated the physical map as confirmed, said Rockstar executives confirmed the next game "will not take 8 years," and described a workforce of more than 4,000 developers that had more than doubled. In fact, the map rests on a single unverified GameStop sign, the executives only said new technology and tools will let them work faster, and Bloomberg reported 4,711 employees, almost double the 2,441 at RDR2's launch.

item.title: GTA 6 on PC Earlier Than Expected? Report Points to an Early 2027 Release
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: What the Behind-the-Scenes Sources Say The information has caught the spotlight in international media. As reported by the portal GamesBeat, which reached…
item.content:encoded:
What the Behind-the-Scenes Sources Say

The information has caught the spotlight in international media. As reported by the portal GamesBeat, which reached out to four anonymous insider sources familiar with the studio's plans, Rockstar projects releasing GTA 6 for PC as early as the first quarter (Q1) of 2027.

The game has its official release confirmed for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on November 19, 2026. If the rumors hold true, PC players would only need to wait a few months to get their hands on the game. This is a significantly shorter timeframe compared to GTA 5, which took about a year and a half to reach computers after its original launch.

Why Earlier on PC?

According to GamesBeat, the reasons include the size of the PC audience, user-generated content tools and Rockstar's purchase of Cfx.re (FiveM).

Separately, some players on fan forums speculate that AI tools, console security flaws or leaks (such as those from the leaker known as CyberLeek) could let the game be quickly "dumped" and emulated on PCs at launch, and that an earlier PC release would reduce that risk. This theory is not part of the GamesBeat report and remains speculation.

Next Steps

So far, neither Rockstar Games nor its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, have officially commented on the reports regarding the PC version. Fans are left to wait for the initial console launch in late 2026 to find out if the trip to Vice City via keyboard and mouse will indeed arrive early.

Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article attributed to GamesBeat the idea that AI tools and fears of unofficial emulated ports pushed Rockstar to speed up the PC version, along with a "funny" remark and a mention of the leaker CyberLeek. In fact, GamesBeat's report mentions none of this; the reasons it gives are the PC audience, user-generated content tools and the purchase of Cfx.re (FiveM).

item.title: The Sound of Leonida: Rockstar reveals first radio stations, star DJs and original GTA 6 album.
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: The First 6 Confirmed Radio Stations Rockstar has released previews of six radio stations, blending the return of Vice City classics with new additions…
item.content:encoded:
The First 6 Confirmed Radio Stations

Rockstar has released previews of six radio stations, blending the return of Vice City classics with new additions focused on the cultural diversity of the state of Leonida. The hosts (DJs) are voiced by massive global music stars:

  • Cocoteo FM: The home of modern Latin music in Leonida (bachata, merengue, dembow, and reggaeton). Hosted by El Martillo (voiced by superstar Bad Bunny) and La Gata (voiced by RaiNao). The confirmed setlist already features "EoO" (Bad Bunny) and "Canalla" (Romeo Santos & El Chaval de la Bachata).

  • Back Country Radio: Focused on "renegade" country, ideal for exploring the Grassrivers swamps. Hosted by MW (voiced by Morgan Wallen), Delta Dawne (voiced by Lana Del Rey), and swamp meteorologist Mud Dog Mike (played by Jeremy Dufrene). Confirmed tracks include classics like "Don't Come Home A-Drinkin'" (Loretta Lynn) and "The Conversation" (Hank Williams, Jr. & Waylon Jennings).

  • AfroBank FM: Focused on African music excellence, from amapiano to 20th-century classics. Hosted by the duo Burna (voiced by Burna Boy) and Palmsy (voiced by Palms Trax). Confirmed songs include "Joha" (Asake) and "Shay'sana" (DJ Lag & Robot Boii ft. Kamo Mphela).

  • The Chamber 106.6: Leonida's heavy metal radio. Hosted by two legends from the band Slayer: DJ Kerry (Kerry King) and DJ Tom (Tom Araya). Perfect for speeding down the highway to the sound of "I" (Black Sabbath), "I'm Broken" (Pantera), and "Raining Blood" (Slayer).

  • Flash FM: The classic pop institution from GTA: Vice City is back. Hosted by Swedish singer Robyn and model Alex Consani. The station will play hits like "Good Ones" (Charli XCX), "Electric Feel" (MGMT), and "Midnight Sun" (Zara Larsson & PinkPantheress).

  • Dirty South Classics: The pure essence of Southern hospitality, focused on regional rap and classic hip-hop. Hosted by rappers Trick Daddy and Trina. Tracks like "Like A Pimp" (David Banner ft. Lil' Flip) and "Born N Raised" (DJ Khaled ft. Trick Daddy, Rick Ross & Pitbull) are already guaranteed.

Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album

In addition to licensed music, there is Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, a collaborative project with Atlantic Records that Rockstar had already announced on September 17, before the radio stations were revealed. The album will feature 34 original tracks created exclusively for the game, aiming to capture the vibrant energy of Vice City.

The company has already released six singles from this project for the public to stream:

  • "That's It" – Yung Lean (feat. Future & Metro Boomin)

  • "RHYNO" – Travis Scott (produced by Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo of Daft Punk)

  • "Sexy Magic" – CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso, PinkPantheress, Fred again.. & Etienne de Crécy

  • "Last Thing You Need" – Morgan Wallen

  • "Macacoa 2000" – Rauw Alejandro

  • "Bright Lights, Big City" – Keith Richards

The album will also feature tracks by artists like Cardi B ("Don't Chart") and Fuerza Regida ("Suzuki").

Innovation: Earbuds and On-Foot Podcasts

One of the most highly praised mechanical additions revealed in this update is how we consume audio in the game. In GTA 6, players won't need to be inside a car to enjoy the soundtrack. Rockstar confirmed that Lucia and Jason will be able to use earbuds connected to their smartphones to listen to radio stations and the game's various new podcasts while exploring the world on foot.

Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article suggested that Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album was announced together with the radio stations. In fact, Rockstar announced the album on September 17, and the stations were revealed on October 8.

item.title: Cyberleek Returns: New 25-Minute GTA 6 Leak Reveals Illegal Racing, Customization, and Explicit Nudity
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: This Thursday (October 8, 2026), the individual responsible for the recent massive Grand Theft Auto VI leaks published a new video featuring nearly 25…
item.content:encoded:
This Thursday (October 8, 2026), the individual responsible for the recent massive Grand Theft Auto VI leaks published a new video featuring nearly 25 minutes of gameplay. Ironically dubbed "GTA 6: Extended Leek", the material is a direct provocation to Rockstar Games' recent official trailer ("An Extended Look") and brings some of the most detailed revelations about mechanics, the open world, and the controversial level of nudity in the highly anticipated title.

Rockstar Games has not yet officially commented on this new incident. Despite the enormous volume of leaked information and the impact on the team, the developer has maintained its original plans to release the game on November 19, 2026, for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, with no changes to the date.

What the 25 Minutes of Gameplay Show

The released video focuses heavily on exploring Vice City and side activities, confirming the functionality of systems highly anticipated by the community.

  • Off-Road Racing and the Thrillbilly Mud Club: Jason and Lucia are introduced to a club dedicated to mud events. The video shows Jason renting a Maibatsu Sanchez motorcycle for $250 to participate in a dirt race.

  • Return of the Midnight Club Style: A major highlight of the leak is the illegal nocturnal street racing (part of the "Hit N Run VC" mission series, linking Salton to Waning Sands). The footage displays checkpoint races using the first-person camera from the vehicle's cockpit.

  • Deep Vehicle Customization: The automotive tuning system seems to have been vastly expanded, now divided into tabs for "pro builds" (pre-tuned), cosmetics, and performance. The performance tab allows players to change the engine, intake, transmission, and add a nitrous system.

  • First-Person Camera: The video confirms the presence of a native first-person mode, covering both driving vehicles and walking around the map.

  • Emergent Encounters: The material illustrates an internal interaction system where Jason and Lucia meet organically across the map and seamlessly perform activities together, without relying on loading screens for missions.

Explicit Nudity and Realistic Physics

One of the aspects that generated the most surprise and discussion on forums was the presence of interactive, full-frontal nudity in the leaked build. Unlike previous titles where adult content was restricted to very specific contexts, Cyberleek demonstrated scenes without any kind of censorship.

The video shows Jason walking through the Monte Kalaga region completely naked, with the game's physics reacting dynamically to his body movements. Furthermore, full cutscenes were shown without restrictions, including a night scene where Lucia performs a base jump naked — recreating an angle seen in the official materials, but without clothes. The recording also features clips of Lucia wearing undergarments on a helipad and the sudden appearance of a tank, indicating that the leaker was using developer menus or cheat codes to access these features.

The Ongoing Threat of Cyberleek

Cyberleek's disappearance in recent weeks had raised expectations that authorities or Take-Two's private investigators had managed to identify him after issuing subpoenas to platforms like Discord. The sudden return and extensive publication prove that the attacker — who previously orchestrated attacks using only a hotel room, a TV, and an Amazon Fire Stick — remains unidentified and has direct access to an advanced build of the game.

Although Cyberleek attempts to frame his actions as a protest in favor of ending digital pre-orders, full offline access, and the defense of physical media, his financial motivation remains evident. Just like in the August attacks, the leak of this new batch of footage was used as a platform to promote a cryptocurrency (meme coin) controlled by the leaker, a scheme that has allegedly already earned him significant amounts of money at the expense of Rockstar's exposure.

item.title: Xbox Strategy Chief Denies GTA 6 Streaming Exclusivity and Rules Out PC Release via Cloud
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: What the Original Report Claimed The discussion began after a report from The Verge claimed that Microsoft had struck an unprecedented deal to secure…
item.content:encoded:
What the Original Report Claimed

The discussion began after a report from The Verge claimed that Microsoft had struck an unprecedented deal to secure exclusive streaming rights for GTA 6 on Xbox Cloud Gaming.

This move would have opened a major loophole in the market: since Rockstar has not yet confirmed a native PC version of the game, cloud access would have allowed PC gamers to play the title on day one without needing to buy a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S.

Xbox's Clarification

Following the rapid spread of the news, Matthew Ball, Xbox's Chief Strategy Officer, used his social media to say the excitement had "led to some misreporting," without naming The Verge. The executive was straightforward in clarifying two key points:

  • End of the exclusivity rumor: The game will not be streamed exclusively through the Xbox Cloud Gaming catalog.

  • PC is left out: The executive guaranteed that GTA 6 will not be available to play on PC via the cloud service.

This statement pours cold water on the PC gaming community, which saw xCloud as their main hope for enjoying the launch simultaneously with console players.

What Still Remains Open

Despite being categorical in dismissing the exclusivity and PC access, Ball's message was careful. He neither confirmed nor denied the possibility of GTA 6 coming to Xbox Cloud Gaming at launch for other devices (such as Smart TVs, mobile phones, and the consoles themselves).

This means the chance of the game joining Microsoft's cloud service from day one still exists—just not in the exclusive, PC-focused format that was initially reported.

Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article called Matthew Ball an "Xbox director" and said he classified The Verge's report as inaccurate. In fact, Ball is Xbox's Chief Strategy Officer, and he wrote about "misreporting" without naming The Verge.

item.title: [CANCELED] Microsoft closes exclusivity deal for GTA 6 streaming on Xbox Cloud Gaming
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: Update: On October 7, Xbox Chief Strategy Officer Matthew Ball denied this report, stating that "the game will not be streaming exclusively or to PC." The…
item.content:encoded:
Update: On October 7, Xbox Chief Strategy Officer Matthew Ball denied this report, stating that "the game will not be streaming exclusively or to PC." The Verge's Tom Warren later said the deal looked more complicated than he had originally reported.

Microsoft seems to have secured one of the biggest strategic advantages of the current console generation. According to information revealed by journalist Tom Warren from The Verge, the company has closed a major deal with Rockstar Games that guarantees the exclusive streaming rights for Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) on Xbox Cloud Gaming (xCloud) right on its launch day.

In practice, this means that Microsoft's cloud service will initially be the only platform capable of running the game remotely. This move promises to cause a profound impact on the market, especially by opening the doors to a massive player base that would otherwise not have access to the new title because they do not own next-gen hardware.

The salvation for PC and the extended life of Xbox One

The streaming exclusivity on xCloud brings immediate relief to a very significant group: PC players. Maintaining its historical release pattern, Rockstar has not yet announced a native version of GTA 6 for computers, officially confirming the game only for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. With this deal, PC owners will be able to play the title via the cloud, bypassing the absence of an official "port" at launch.

The news also becomes a huge asset for those who still own an Xbox One. The last-generation console does not have the firepower to run GTA 6 natively, but thanks to compatibility with Xbox Cloud Gaming, users will be able to stream the game directly from Microsoft's servers. This reach of the Xbox brand will also extend to compatible smartphones, tablets, and Smart TVs.

Changes to Xbox Cloud and the new "pay-per-use"

The leak of this deal is no coincidence and aligns with a vital restructuring phase of Microsoft's cloud service. The company is preparing major changes to Xbox Cloud Gaming starting in November, including a model that goes beyond the traditional Game Pass subscription.

In this new "pay-per-use" format, Microsoft will allow users who are not Game Pass subscribers to buy streaming hours to play titles from their own digital library. It is worth reinforcing a crucial detail: being available for streaming on xCloud does not mean that GTA 6 will be added for free to the Game Pass catalog. The most likely scenario is that players will need to purchase the game on the Microsoft store in order to stream it.

Xbox also officially announced on September 3 that it will start setting monthly cloud hour limits depending on the user's subscription tier: 15 hours per month for Game Pass Ultimate, 10 for Premium and 5 for Essential. To binge-play a colossal game like GTA 6, the feature of purchasing additional hours will be a central pillar in this new platform economy.

What remains to be discovered?
Despite the strength of the sources heard by The Verge, some crucial commercial details remain confidential. The main one is the duration of this exclusivity window. It is unknown for how long Xbox Cloud Gaming will be the only place to stream the game before competitors (like GeForce Now or PlayStation's streaming) can enter the fray.

Another challenge Microsoft will need to face is infrastructure: supporting the massive server congestion at the launch of the most anticipated entertainment product of the decade.

Until there is an official announcement detailing how it works, players wait anxiously. If everything is confirmed, Microsoft will not only have leveraged Xbox console sales, but will have transformed virtually any internet-connected screen into a direct passport to Vice City.

Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article did not reflect Xbox's denial and described the monthly cloud hour limits as a rumor. In fact, Matthew Ball denied the streaming exclusivity and PC streaming on October 7, and Xbox officially announced the 15/10/5-hour limits on September 3.

item.title: GTA VI: The Quest for Survival and the End of Extras in Leonida
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: In an exclusive interview with LOVE Magazine released today, the Rockstar North team opened up about the design philosophies and themes that will guide…
item.content:encoded:
In an exclusive interview with LOVE Magazine released today, the Rockstar North team opened up about the design philosophies and themes that will guide Grand Theft Auto VI. With a deep focus on the dynamic between protagonists Jason and Lucia, the studio indicated that the franchise's next iteration won't just aim to impress with its sheer scale, but will revolutionize how players interact with the world of Leonida.

The "American Dream" Deconstructed

If in previous titles players controlled cartel leaders, mobsters seeking glory, or bank robbers obsessed with unimaginable fortunes, the central duo in GTA VI has much more grounded ambitions.

The criminal life in Leonida isn't driven by a desire for ostentation and control of the underworld, but by the sheer need for survival. Jason and Lucia's goal is straightforward: clear their debts, achieve financial stability, and secure a home for their family. This deconstruction of the classic GTA "American Dream" promises to deliver a more intimate and relatable narrative arc.

The Perfectly Imperfect Dynamic

The magazine also delved into the protagonists' psyches, detailing how they complement each other through their contrasts:

  • Lucia: Making history as the franchise's first playable female protagonist with an active voice and storyline, she is described as an unstoppable force. Determined and uncompromising, Lucia is the engine that drives the duo forward, refusing to let problems halt her pursuit of a better life.

  • Jason: Serving as the perfect counterweight, Jason has a much more reactive profile. His actions and choices are frequently shaped by the chaos, circumstances, and events happening around him.

Rockstar's writers emphasized that both were developed as highly human figures—vulnerable and deeply flawed. They aren't absolute heroes or villains, but people who are "sometimes right, sometimes wrong," and who will evolve by learning from each other throughout their journey.

Fun Always Above Realism

Another major point of debate among fans has always been the balance between GTA's classic arcade gameplay and the hyper-realism seen in Red Dead Redemption 2. Rob Nelson, Co-Head of Rockstar North, confirmed the new game's direction: fun dictates the rules.

The state of Leonida will be the stage for unpredictable events, chaos, humor, and classic biting American satire. Realism will be applied surgically, existing solely to amplify player immersion. If a highly realistic mechanic makes the experience tedious or less fluid, it will be scrapped in favor of gameplay and fun.

Despite prioritizing the playful aspect, the technical ambition for the open world remains unprecedented. Narrative director James Horton made a bold promise regarding the map's inhabitants, stating that "nobody you meet is an extra." He was talking about character writing, not artificial intelligence: pedestrians are written as full characters, with a dedicated team in Los Angeles writing their dialogue, because "everyone you meet is the main character in their own story."

Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article said Lucia was the first such protagonist "in 28 years" and presented the "nobody you meet is an extra" quote as a sign of a leap in AI. In fact, no source gives the 28-year figure, and the quote is from narrative director James Horton, about how characters and pedestrians are written.

item.title: The Clash of Two Eras: Capcom Is Preparing a 'Crossover' Between Resident Evil Timelines
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: According to producer Jun Takeuchi, the development team has been actively mapping out the exact moment when the saga's past and present will perfectly…
item.content:encoded:
According to producer Jun Takeuchi, the development team has been actively mapping out the exact moment when the saga's past and present will perfectly align. The executive has categorized this narrative convergence as a true internal "crossover" for the franchise.

Historically, the modern Resident Evil era has operated under a clear dual strategy:

  • The Present Timeline: Titles like Resident Evil 7: Biohazard, Resident Evil Village, and Resident Evil: Requiem focus on pushing the overarching story forward. These games introduce new threats, fresh protagonists like Ethan Winters, and the latest developments in modern bioterrorism.

  • The Past Timeline: The reimagined classics (Resident Evil 2, 3, and 4 Remakes) serve not only to modernize gameplay but to tie up loose ends in the original lore, re-establishing the weight of classic figures and corporations with newfound narrative depth.

Resident Evil: Requiem, released in early 2026, is part of the preparation for this convergence, not its culmination. According to Takeuchi, Requiem's references to Umbrella and Spencer and the return of Raccoon City are groundwork for a future crossover, which will come once the remakes catch up with the era of the numbered games.

The game resurrected the foundational ghosts of the series by sending veteran Leon S. Kennedy and new protagonist, FBI analyst Grace Ashcroft, back into the ruins of Raccoon City—including a chilling return to the iconic R.P.D. station. The plot delivered direct references to the all-powerful Umbrella Corporation and its enigmatic founder, Oswell E. Spencer, seamlessly bridging the classic legacy with entirely new survival threats.

This strategic move confirmed that the recent remakes were never just an exercise in nostalgia; they were crucial pieces of a much larger puzzle. By reintroducing players to the horrors of Raccoon City and Umbrella in the remakes, Capcom laid the perfect groundwork for those same threats to haunt the modern story arc, groundwork that continued in the highly acclaimed Requiem and whose meaning, according to Takeuchi, should become clear before the series' 40th anniversary.

Now, fans must wait to see how classic veterans and the new generation of survivors will continue to collide in this ambitious narrative roadmap.

Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article said the crossover between Resident Evil's timelines materialized and culminated in Requiem. In fact, Jun Takeuchi described Requiem as preparation for a future crossover, when the remakes catch up with the numbered games, with its meaning to become clear before the series' 40th anniversary.

item.title: Hurricanes and Storms: The Impressive New Weather System in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: According to Owen Shepherd, Rockstar's Vice President of Art for Lighting and Rendering, the team has completely rebuilt the weather system to make it…
item.content:encoded:
According to Owen Shepherd, Rockstar's Vice President of Art for Lighting and Rendering, the team has completely rebuilt the weather system to make it much more localized and persistent, achieving a scale never before seen in the franchise.

Check out the main highlights of the newly confirmed weather and storm mechanics:

  • Hurricanes and Tropical Storms

    The game will feature the extreme weather phenomena that are a trademark of Florida. During these powerful storms, players will face torrential rain, heavy winds, thunder, and lightning, with water realistically running off roofs and utility poles along the streets.

  • Localized and Dynamic Weather

    The new system features fully dynamic cloudscapes, allowing you to actually see storms moving across the map. It will be perfectly possible to stand in a dry, sunny area while watching heavy rain fall in the distance in another region of Leonida.

  • New Wind System

    The wind will affect the open world in incredibly immersive ways. The game will feature different patterns of air currents, such as offshore breezes after sunset and convective updrafts. In practice, wind gusts will blow hair and debris around, create ripples on the water's surface, and bend the tall grass in the swamps.

  • Persistent Visual Impact

    Rain will leave real marks on the environment even after the storm has passed. Lasting puddles will remain on the roads indicating the exact path of the storm, and rainbows can form depending on the precise sunlight and humidity conditions.

This impressive attention to detail reinforces Rockstar's goal of creating a much more reactive open world. Nature in Leonida won't just serve as a static backdrop, but rather as an active, unpredictable, and shifting force during Jason and Lucia's daily routines and explorations.

Stay tuned to our website for more updates and full coverage as soon as new information about GTA 6 emerges!

Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article mentioned "volumetric clouds" and "sea breezes after sunset." In fact, Rockstar's Owen Shepherd described fully dynamic cloudscapes, offshore breezes after sunset and convective updrafts.

item.title: GTA 6 Wildlife Blowout: Over 170 Species, Legendary Animals, and Next-Gen Fur Physics Revealed
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: According to the new details, players will share the open world with over 170 different species of animals, breathing life into the skies, swamps…
item.content:encoded:
According to the new details, players will share the open world with over 170 different species of animals, breathing life into the skies, swamps, forests, and oceans of Vice City and its surrounding counties.

Here is the breakdown of the wildlife populations confirmed so far:

  • 60+ types of birds

  • 30+ land mammals

  • A diverse array of fish and reptiles

A Next-Generation Ocean Ecosystem

The waters of Leonida won't just be for high-speed jet ski races. Michael Kane, Vice President of Dynamic Art at Rockstar Games, confirmed that the game’s marine life has received a massive overhaul.

Players will encounter various species of sharks, whales, rays, sea turtles, and jellyfish. Kane emphasized that each of these marine animals is built with entirely distinct movement behaviors, ensuring the ocean feels as dynamic and unpredictable as the city streets.

Groundbreaking Visuals and Fur Physics

Rockstar is pushing their proprietary engine to its absolute limits for the game's fauna. The article confirms that animals will feature advanced lighting interactions, including iridescence, bioluminescence, and translucency—perfect for the neon-lit waters or the murky depths of the swamps.

Furthermore, GTA 6 introduces an entirely new hair and fur simulation system. Animal pelts are now fully simulated and will dynamically react to the environment. Expect to see fur react realistically to water, get caked in mud and dirt, and even experience matting and clumping over time.

Legendary Animals (and a Possible Compendium)

For fans who spent hundreds of hours tracking and studying wildlife in Red Dead Redemption 2, there is incredible news. The GTA 6 animal roster size sits right alongside RDR2's base count of 178 species.

Hunting and cataloging have not been confirmed, and neither has an in-game Compendium where players scan animals to register them; for now, those ideas are speculation. What the report does confirm is that wildlife will be divided into different rarity tiers:

  • Discoverable

  • Rare

  • Legendary

Rockstar has not revealed which animals are Legendary, but whether you are tracking rare wildlife through the Leonida brush, visiting the newly confirmed in-game Zoos, or just trying to avoid gators in the swamplands, it's clear that the wildlife in GTA 6 is going to be a game within the game.

Stay tuned as we continue to break down all the latest GTA 6 news and leaks!

Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article called Michael Kane GTA 6's Animation Director and presented hunting, an in-game Compendium for scanning animals and a Legendary Panther as confirmed. In fact, Kane is Rockstar's Vice President of Dynamic Art, and only the Discoverable, Rare and Legendary tiers are confirmed; Rockstar has not revealed which animals are Legendary.

item.title: GTA 6 Confirmed Side Activities: From Kayaking to Zoo Visits!
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: The newly confirmed list of minigames and side activities proves Rockstar Games is laser-focused on delivering their most immersive and lived-in open…
item.content:encoded:
The newly confirmed list of minigames and side activities proves Rockstar Games is laser-focused on delivering their most immersive and lived-in open world to date.

Here are the side activities confirmed so far (Game Informer notes the list is only partial):

  • Base jumping: Classic skydiving returns, offering the perfect way to take advantage of Vice City's towering skyline.

  • Billiards: Leonida’s dive bars could feature pool tables where you can kick back and relax; whether you can hustle locals for cash hasn't been revealed.

  • Gyms: The beloved workout system is back, heavily hinting that physical character customization—a fan-favorite feature from GTA: San Andreas—is making a return.

  • Kayaking: Possibly a quiet, low-key way to navigate the dense, winding swamps and rivers outside the city limits.

  • Mini Golf: The ultimate downtime distraction between intense story missions.

  • Scuba diving: Leonida’s ocean floor could be rich in detail; shipwreck exploration and deep-sea scavenging would be natural fits, but Rockstar hasn't confirmed them.

  • Street and off-road racing: The core DNA of the franchise lives on with underground sprint races on the asphalt and mud-kicking rallies in the backcountry.

  • Zoos: A highly unexpected first for the series. While we don't know the full extent of our interaction with the animals yet, it adds an entirely new layer of life to the map.

  • Air boating: The quintessential Florida-inspired vehicle, perfect for tearing across gator-infested swamplands like the Everglades.

  • Jet skiing: High-speed coastal racing and exploration across Vice City's pristine beaches.

This diverse lineup shows the new game will lean heavily into the local culture of the state, perfectly blending chaotic urban life with wild, untamed nature. The specific additions of airboats, zoos, and kayaking suggest that Leonida's wildlife and waterways will play a massive role in the player's day-to-day experience.

Keep it locked right here for full coverage and updates the second more GTA 6 news drops!

Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article presented the list as every side activity and described details such as hustling locals at pool, stealthy kayaking and shipwreck exploration as facts. In fact, Game Informer notes the list is partial and only named the activities; those details are not confirmed.

item.title: GTA 6 Collector's Box Revealed: What's Inside the $399.99 Goodtime State – Vice City Collection
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: Rockstar Games revealed on Thursday, September 24, 2026 the first collector's product for Grand Theft Auto VI: The Goodtime State – Vice City Collection …
item.content:encoded:
Rockstar Games revealed on Thursday, September 24, 2026 the first collector's product for Grand Theft Auto VI: The Goodtime State – Vice City Collection. Sold through the Rockstar Store for $399.99 (also listed at £349.99, €399.99 and CA$559.99), the box is limited to one per customer.

The collection is built around the Leonida Keys and Vice City, the two regions where Jason and Lucia's story takes place, and every item is officially licensed merchandise themed after the game's fictional version of Florida.

Check out everything inside the box:

  • Macca the gator figure

    A collectible statue of the gator mascot seen across Leonida, with a twist-open base.

  • Oakley® Frogskins™ sunglasses

    A themed pair of the classic Oakley frames, matching the beach look of the Keys.

  • New Era® 9FORTY cap

    An adjustable cap with Leonida branding.

  • Leonida Keys crossbody bag

    A shoulder bag inspired by the island chain where Jason starts the game.

  • Small collectibles

    A Macca the gator magnetic mirror, a Chunkee the Manatee shot glass, a collectible Vice City swizzle spoon and a razor-blade keychain.

  • Pins, stickers and poster

    A set of nine Leonida Keys enamel pins in a metal tin, a sticker pack and a double-sided souvenir poster with the map of Leonida.

Important: the game is NOT included. The Goodtime State is a merchandise box only, with no download code. GTA VI itself is sold separately and launches on November 19, 2026 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, so a fan who wants both the box and the standard edition of the game should budget close to $480.

Fan reaction was mixed, mostly because of the price and the missing game. For collectors, though, it is the most complete set of official Leonida merchandise Rockstar has released so far, and the map poster is one of the first physical looks at the state's full layout.

item.title: Is the GTA 6 Map Bigger Than Leonida? An Old Puerto Rico Rumor Resurfaces After the 192GB Leak
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: Ever since the 192GB archive of old Rockstar material surfaced online on September 18, 2026, fans have been combing through early GTA 6 map files, which…
item.content:encoded:
Ever since the 192GB archive of old Rockstar material surfaced online on September 18, 2026, fans have been combing through early GTA 6 map files, which Kotaku dates to around 2015 (only MMOCulture mentions 2014). Among the theories spreading in the community, an old one has resurfaced: a fan rumor, first posted on 4chan in 2021, about an island inspired by Puerto Rico, which would point to a playable area outside the state of Leonida.

The idea is not new for the series. In GTA 5, the snowy town of North Yankton appeared only in specific story missions, far from Los Santos. Fans suggest a Caribbean island could play a similar role in GTA 6, especially because of Lucia's Latin roots.

Here is what we know, and what we don't:

  • What is confirmed

    Rockstar has only officially presented the state of Leonida, with six regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia and Mount Kalaga.

  • What the leak shows

    Outlets that analysed the archive describe an early Leonida prototype, with labels such as "Alligator Farm", "Coast Guard" and "Disused Theme Park", plus early Vice City assets.

  • What remains unverified

    None of the outlets we checked mention a Puerto Rico-style island. The theory is an old fan rumor from 2021, not something found in the leaked files.

  • Why caution matters

    The files are about a decade old. Even the coverage of the leak stresses that a prototype of that age cannot confirm the final map's roads, borders or playable locations.

That is why this story carries our Rumor badge. An extra island, accessed only during a mission, would be a fun surprise and fits Rockstar's history, but there is no official sign of it. Rockstar has not commented on the leak.

GTA VI launches November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Until then, everything confirmed about the state is in our guide: the GTA 6 map and Leonida's regions.

Stay tuned to our website for more updates and full coverage as soon as new information about GTA 6 emerges!

Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article said fans had found renders of a Puerto Rico-style island in leaked files dated to around 2014–2015. In fact, the Puerto Rico idea is an old fan rumor from 4chan (2021) that no reputable outlet has linked to the leak, and Kotaku dates the map to around 2015.

item.title: 192GB Rockstar Leak Surfaces: Cancelled GTA 5 Liberty City DLC, Agent Trevor and Early GTA 6 Assets
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: About 192GB of internal Rockstar Games data surfaced online on September 18, 2026, two months before the launch of GTA 6. The files are not new: they are…
item.content:encoded:
About 192GB of internal Rockstar Games data surfaced online on September 18, 2026, two months before the launch of GTA 6. The files are not new: they are linked to the security breach Rockstar suffered in 2022, part of which had already leaked as GTA 5 source code in December 2023. The full archive circulated privately for years and has only now been shared widely.

Despite the timing, most of the material is about GTA 5, not GTA 6. Dataminers in the community, such as TJGM, have been sharing their findings, though many of them have not been independently verified.

Check out the main highlights reported so far:

  • Cancelled Liberty City expansion for GTA 5

    Files for a single-player DLC that would have brought Liberty City to GTA 5, with a map reportedly larger than the version seen in GTA 4.

  • "Agent Trevor" DLC

    A cancelled secret-agent expansion starring Trevor, with dozens of missions and assets that include spaceship interiors and space suits.

  • Cut endings and missions

    An alternate, more brutal death for Trevor in one of GTA 5's endings, and a cut mission pairing Franklin with Brucie, the GTA 4 character.

  • Beta content

    Dialogue and vehicles from GTA 5's development that never made it into the final game.

  • Early GTA 6 assets

    Very early, low-detail models and map blockouts of Vice City and Leonida, dated to around 2014–2015 and reportedly built with GTA 5's tools.

That last point is what drew the most attention, but it says little about the game coming in November. As the coverage of the leak stresses, blockouts this old do not represent the final map, which has been rebuilt many times since.

Following our editorial policy, we report that the leak happened, but we do not show or link to the leaked material. Rockstar has not commented on this archive. GTA VI launches November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

Stay tuned to our website for more updates and full coverage as soon as new information about GTA 6 emerges!

item.title: Stephen Root Confirms He's in GTA 6, Widely Believed to Voice Brian Heder: "You're Gonna See Me in There"
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: American actor Stephen Root has confirmed that he is in Grand Theft Auto VI, making him the first member of the cast to publicly go on record about a role…
item.content:encoded:
American actor Stephen Root has confirmed that he is in Grand Theft Auto VI, making him the first member of the cast to publicly go on record about a role in the game. He did not name his character, but fans and the press, who recognized his voice, widely believe he plays Brian Heder. Root spoke to the Associated Press at the BAFTA TV Tea Party in mid-September 2026.

Asked about GTA 6, he did not dodge the question: "You're gonna see me in there." He also admitted that keeping the secret had become almost impossible, because fans had already recognized him: "There were too many people that knew me from King of the Hill and my voice."

Check out what we know about the actor and his character:

  • Who is Brian Heder

    According to Rockstar's official profile, Brian is an old-school drug runner in the Leonida Keys who lets Jason live in one of his properties in exchange for help with his business. In other words, he is one of the first people players will meet, since the story begins in the Keys.

  • Who is Stephen Root

    A veteran character actor known as Milton in Office Space, Monroe Fuches in Barry, and the voices of Bill Dauterive and Buck Strickland in the animated series King of the Hill.

  • How fans found out

    Players began linking the voice to Root as soon as Brian was introduced in the second trailer, in May 2025. The Extended Look shown in August 2026 gave him more screen time and turned the guess into near-certainty.

  • What is still a secret

    Rockstar has not officially announced the cast, and the actors behind Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos remain unconfirmed.

Root's comments suggest the studio is relaxing its famously tight secrecy as launch approaches. More cast reveals, official or not, are likely in the coming weeks. Meet the rest of the characters in our guide: Jason, Lucia and the GTA 6 cast.

GTA VI launches November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

Stay tuned to our website for more updates and full coverage as soon as new information about GTA 6 emerges!

Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article said Stephen Root confirmed he plays Brian Heder. In fact, Root confirmed he is in the game but did not name his character; the link to Brian Heder comes from fans and the press, who recognized his voice.

item.title: GTA 6 Daily Life Detailed: A Physical Phone, a Shared Hideout and Protected Story Locations
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: With 65 days to go until launch, Rockstar keeps revealing how life in Leonida will work between missions. In a long interview with the Japanese magazine…
item.content:encoded:
With 65 days to go until launch, Rockstar keeps revealing how life in Leonida will work between missions. In a long interview with the Japanese magazine Famitsu, translated into English by GTAVice, Rob Nelson, head of development and co-studio head at Rockstar North, described the small systems that make Jason and Lucia's routine feel lived-in.

The common thread is realism: objects exist physically in the world, the couple's home behaves like a real home, and the open world respects the needs of the story.

Check out the main highlights of the new details:

  • A phone you actually hold

    The cell phone is now a physical object in Jason and Lucia's hands instead of a flat 2D overlay, as it was in GTA V. Rockstar mentioned apps for video, fitness tracking, banking, social media and "Scooter Bros", a vehicle delivery service.

  • Photos, but no posting

    Jason and Lucia can send photos to each other. Because both are on the run, though, they cannot upload anything to social media; they can only follow other accounts.

  • A home that feels shared

    The hideout is treated as a place where two people live. In the demo shown to Famitsu, Jason pulls back the covers and climbs into bed next to a sleeping Lucia. You also can't toss objects anywhere: Nelson explained that a mug has to be carried to a place where it can properly be put down.

  • Protected story locations

    As in Red Dead Redemption 2, some places that matter to the story are off-limits for crime. Nelson's example: you can't steal cars outside the strip club owned by Jason's friend Dre'Quan, so players can't accidentally ruin a location the story still needs.

  • A body to look after

    How you play changes Jason and Lucia's bodies. Training builds muscle, overeating can make them gain weight, and food gives temporary boosts to their health and stamina meters.

Together, these details point to a slower, more grounded GTA, closer to the daily rhythm of Red Dead Redemption 2 than to the arcade feel of earlier games. For everything confirmed about money, gyms and hideouts, read our guide: GTA 6 gameplay: money, gym and hideouts.

GTA VI launches November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

Stay tuned to our website for more updates and full coverage as soon as new information about GTA 6 emerges!

item.title: Miami Beach Votes to Negotiate GTA 6 Marketing Deal: 'Vice City' Beach Ads Proposed From October 15
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: Vice City is about to take over the real Miami Beach. On September 10, 2026, the Miami Beach City Commission voted 4–3 to authorize negotiations on a…
item.content:encoded:
Vice City is about to take over the real Miami Beach. On September 10, 2026, the Miami Beach City Commission voted 4–3 to authorize negotiations on a marketing deal that would bring Grand Theft Auto VI branding to the city's beaches ahead of the game's launch. As of October 12, the contract had still not been signed, according to reporter Joel Franco via GTA BOOM.

The approval came after a heated debate. Commissioner David Suarez opposed the deal, showed footage from the game during the session and said he did not want the city's brand associated with it. Separately, Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz had criticized a different GTA 6 promotion proposed to Miami-Dade County, pointing to the series' focus on crime. Supporters, like Commissioner Monica Matteo-Salinas, argued that enjoying fiction is not the same as endorsing crime, and stressed the financial benefit for the city.

Check out the main proposed terms of the campaign:

  • Where the ads will appear

    Only on private beach equipment, the chairs and umbrellas run by the concessionaire Boucher Brothers. No Rockstar branding will go on city property such as lifeguard stands.

  • What they will show

    The ads are limited to the Roman numeral "VI" and the name "Vice City", described as discreet placements.

  • When

    The proposal calls for October 15 to December 31, 2026, covering the November 19 launch and the holiday season, but with the contract still unsigned, the start date will likely slip.

  • How much

    Reports put the value of the deal in the millions of dollars, with Beebom citing about $3 million.

The campaign is not limited to the beach. On September 14, a photo shared on Reddit showed large advertising panels laid out behind the Kaseya Center, the Miami Heat's arena in downtown Miami, which turned out to form a "Welcome to Vice City" sign. It was installed on the arena's roof on September 22 as part of a separate $975,000 deal with Miami-Dade County.

Miami is the real-world inspiration for Vice City, and Rockstar seems ready to make the most of it. If you are in Florida this fall, expect to see the city and the game blend together. To learn how Vice City fits into the state of Leonida, read our guide: the GTA 6 map and Leonida's regions.

Stay tuned to our website for more updates and full coverage as soon as new information about GTA 6 emerges!

Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article said Miami Beach approved the deal, that the sheriff criticized it and that the Kaseya Center sign would read "Welcome to VI." In fact, the 4–3 vote only authorized negotiations, the contract was still unsigned as of October 12, the sheriff criticized a separate Miami-Dade County proposal, and the sign reads "Welcome to Vice City."

item.title: Rockstar Explains GTA 6's Two Protagonists, Gyms and New Wanted System in Famitsu Interview
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: In an interview with the Japanese magazine Famitsu , Rob Nelson , head of development and co-studio head at Rockstar North, gave one of the most detailed…
item.content:encoded:
In an interview with the Japanese magazine Famitsu, Rob Nelson, head of development and co-studio head at Rockstar North, gave one of the most detailed explanations yet of how Grand Theft Auto VI plays. He covered how Jason and Lucia's relationship works, the return of gyms and a police system rebuilt from scratch. Here are the highlights, organized by topic.

Jason and Lucia: characters and relationship

Rockstar first considered four playable characters, but settled on two. According to Nelson, the team learned with Arthur Morgan in Red Dead Redemption 2 that fewer protagonists means more screen time for each one and a stronger emotional bond with the player.

  • Partners in crime or a couple: Players choose how to treat the relationship. Skipping the romance closes off some interactions, such as holding hands or kissing, but the main story can be completed either way.
  • Switching characters: You can switch freely between Jason and Lucia in the open world, except at specific story moments. In one specific early mission, set in a high-rise housing complex, control is locked to Jason.
  • Hideouts that change: As with the camp in RDR2, the story is told in chapters, and the couple's hideout changes as it progresses.

Gyms are back

  • Body stats: The game tracks each character's health, stamina and fitness. Depending on your habits, they can gain muscle or body fat.
  • Workouts: Gym minigames return, as in GTA San Andreas. Leveling up takes consistency: Rockstar described a routine of three exercises a day for three days in a row.
  • Food: Eating gives temporary boosts to health and stamina on top of the base values you raise by training.

A smarter wanted system

  • Witnesses: As in RDR2, a crime only reaches the police if someone sees it and reports it.
  • Cash vs. bank: Money now works like GTA Online. Cash you carry is lost if you die or get arrested; money deposited in the bank is safe.
  • Criminal profile: The game evaluates what kind of criminal you are, for example a professional one or a violent and dangerous one.
  • No more invisible rifles: Long guns are now visible on your character and must be stored at Ammu-Nation or in a car trunk to stay discreet.

Taken together, the interview shows a GTA built around consequences: what you eat, where you keep your money and who sees you all matter. For the full breakdown of the police system, read our guide: the GTA 6 wanted system.

GTA VI launches November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

Stay tuned to our website for more updates and full coverage as soon as new information about GTA 6 emerges!

Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article said control is locked to Jason at the very start of the game and that the criminal profile can push you into a "chaotic state." In fact, the lock applies to one specific early mission, and the criminal profile evaluates what kind of criminal you are, such as professional or violent.

item.title: GTA 6 Limited-Edition DualSense Controllers Open for Pre-Order at $84.99
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: Pre-orders for the Grand Theft Auto VI limited-edition DualSense controllers opened on September 10, 2026, at 7:00 a.m. PT (10:00 a.m. ET) in the United…
item.content:encoded:
Pre-orders for the Grand Theft Auto VI limited-edition DualSense controllers opened on September 10, 2026, at 7:00 a.m. PT (10:00 a.m. ET) in the United States and at 10:00 a.m. local time in the UK and Europe. Sony first revealed the two designs during the PlayStation State of Play on September 3.

Each controller costs $84.99 (¥12,480 in Japan) and ships on November 19, 2026, the same day the game launches on PlayStation 5.

Check out the main details of each version:

  • White Limited Edition

    Pastel tones inspired by "Vice City at daybreak", with a sun-bleached beach look. It is sold on PlayStation Direct and at participating retailers worldwide.

  • Black Limited Edition

    A black body with shimmering neon-purple gradients that evoke Vice City at night. In the US, the UK and several European countries, including Spain, France, Germany and Italy, it is exclusive to PlayStation Direct.

  • Shared details

    Both feature palm tree shapes on the grips, the GTA VI logo on the touchpad, purple face buttons and D-pad, and the Rockstar logo on the back.

  • Same hardware

    Inside, they are standard DualSense controllers. There are no performance upgrades and nothing is unlocked in the game; the price reflects the cosmetic design only.

Themed controllers tend to sell out quickly, and the black version, available only on Sony's store in many countries, is the one most likely to disappear first. If you want one for launch day, pre-ordering is the safest bet; you can find the US listing for the black edition on PlayStation Direct, linked in the sources below.

item.title: GTA 6's New HUD Makes Losing the Cops Harder: No More Police Dots on the Minimap
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: The GTA 6 Extended Look , shown on Netflix in August 2026, made one thing clear: Rockstar has completely redesigned the game's HUD, and the change hits…
item.content:encoded:
The GTA 6 Extended Look, shown on Netflix in August 2026, made one thing clear: Rockstar has completely redesigned the game's HUD, and the change hits hardest where veterans feel it most — escaping the police.

For years, the trick in Grand Theft Auto was simple: watch the minimap, avoid the red dots and their vision cones, and wait for the stars to fade. In GTA 6, that safety net is gone.

Check out the main changes to the wanted system's HUD:

  • No more "all-seeing" minimap

    The classic red dots showing each officer's exact position and line of sight have disappeared. Instead, a flashing red-and-blue zone marks the general area where the police are searching for you. Rockstar calls this state Heat.

  • Hanger icon — your clothes

    Shows that the police know what you are wearing. Changing outfits becomes a real way to throw them off.

  • Face icon — your identity

    Shows whether a witness or a security camera has identified you, or whether a mask kept your face hidden.

  • Vehicle icon — your getaway car

    Lets you know if the cops or cameras have identified the car you are using.

  • Partner icon — your accomplice

    Shows whether the police know you had someone with you during the crime, which matters in a game built around Jason and Lucia working as a pair.

In practice, the HUD now tells you what the police know, not where they are. To find officers, you have to look around, use cover and blend into traffic. Rockstar's Rob Nelson later added in an interview with Famitsu that crimes depend on witnesses, while the Extended Look, shown on August 27, revealed a wanted meter with room for six stars.

It is a big shift for a series that made fleeing the cops almost routine. Expect getaways to take more planning: masks, a change of clothes and a backup car may be as important as a fast engine. For tips on how to lose the police based on everything Rockstar has shown, read our guide: the GTA 6 wanted system.

GTA VI launches November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

Stay tuned to our website for more updates and full coverage as soon as new information about GTA 6 emerges!

Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article said Rob Nelson mentioned a six-star wanted scale in his Famitsu interview. In fact, the six stars were shown in the Extended Look on August 27; the Famitsu interview covered the role of witnesses.

item.title: The GTA 6 Effect: PS5 Pro Sells Out Across the US and Console Sales Jump After the Extended Look
item.dc:creator: VICEVERSA
item.description: Grand Theft Auto VI isn't out yet, but it is already moving the hardware market. Since the Extended Look premiered on Netflix in late August 2026, demand…
item.content:encoded:
Grand Theft Auto VI isn't out yet, but it is already moving the hardware market. Since the Extended Look premiered on Netflix in late August 2026, demand for consoles has spiked, and the PS5 Pro has become the hardest machine to find in the United States.

By mid-September, the PS5 Pro was listed as out of stock at Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, Target and PlayStation Direct, with GameStop offering only limited pre-owned units in some locations.

Check out the main numbers behind the "GTA 6 effect":

  • Official price vs. resale

    The PS5 Pro officially costs $899.99, after Sony raised it from $749.99 in an increase announced on March 27, 2026 and effective April 2, citing "continued pressures in the global economic landscape" (the press linked the hike to higher memory costs). Third-party sellers took advantage of the shortage, with listings above $1,300 on Amazon and one Walmart marketplace listing asking $1,469, roughly 60% above the official price.

  • Sales spike in the UK

    According to NielsenIQ data reported by The Game Business, PlayStation 5 sales in the UK rose about 33% and Xbox Series X|S sales about 34% in the week after the Extended Look.

  • Not just PlayStation

    Xbox consoles saw the same boost, which makes sense: GTA 6 launches only on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, with no PC version announced.

Analysts urge caution, though. Newzoo's Ronan Patrick noted that a short-term spike does not guarantee lasting growth in console ownership, especially with hardware prices this high.

Our advice: if you still need a console for launch day, buy from official retailers and avoid inflated marketplace listings. Restocks tend to arrive in waves as November approaches. Not sure which edition of the game to get? Read our guide: GTA 6 editions, prices and pre-orders.

GTA VI launches November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

Stay tuned to our website for more updates and full coverage as soon as new information about GTA 6 emerges!

Correction (October 16, 2026): an earlier version of this article said the PS5 Pro's price rose from $699 and that Sony cited higher memory costs. In fact, it rose from $749.99 to $899.99 (announced March 27, effective April 2, 2026), and Sony cited global economic pressures; the link to memory costs was the press's reading.
